changes.notes: Round 5 fixes on payee accounts F5-F7, dark. Webhook intake: a retryable refusal (amount short, order not yet awaiting payment, unknown order inside a 10 minute grace window) answers 409 and does NOT store the event id, so the gateway retry is judged again; permanent refusals (wrong payee, currency mismatch, draft payee with no snapshot or a live order, unknown order after the grace window, same payee and gateway order id in two tenants) are stored once as ignored. Order lookup is filtered by payee in the SQL. Bad signatures write at most one chained audit row per payee per minute (with the count of the minute before) and are answered 429 after 20 a minute per payee; good calls are not counted. Owner call nonces are pruned after the 5 minute window and the owner key is limited to 60 calls a minute. The audit order test now checks an explicit newest-first list. No money behaviour changed, nothing deployed, no flag changed.

Payee accounts F5 (owner scope), F6 (owner API routes) and F7 (webhook intake per payee), dark behind MNP_PAYEE_ACCOUNTS. One owner-role check (requireOwner) now guards every payee and route change and the new owner-only audit view and chain check. Owner routes under /v1/owner (list, read, create, edit, activate, pause, retire, set route, check secret presence, audit, audit verify) are thin calls to the existing functions, signed with the master secret (time, nonce, method, path, body; each nonce works once); keys of every tenant class are refused. New POST /v1/webhooks/payee/{id}: the signature is checked with that payee's webhook secret on the raw body, an event id is kept once per payee, and the payment is applied by the same code as rail confirm against the order's own payee (never today's route). Unknown order, other payee, other event types and mismatched amounts are stored as ignored (answer 200) and never credit. Paused and retired payees still accept payments; a draft payee accepts only test orders. Contract file regenerated. No real gateway call, no flag changed, money flag stays OFF, nothing deployed.

Payee accounts F3 (routing and order snapshot) and F4 (gateway adapters), dark behind MNP_PAYEE_ACCOUNTS. With the flag on, buy_credits takes an optional product, picks the payee from payee_route (product row, else the * row, else no_route 503; paused or wrong-currency main payee uses the fallback if active, else payee_unavailable 503) and copies payee id, route, version, mode and a snapshot onto the order for good. A fallback use leaves an audit row and an owner alert. setRoute (owner only) refuses overlap and non-active payees. Gateway adapter interface with a Razorpay adapter (create order, verify signature, refund; injected fetch and secret reader, nothing calls the real gateway) and a fake adapter. Nothing in credits, lots, holds or the ledger chain reads the payee. Not wired yet: processRail still uses the old rail (F7/F9). No flag changed, nothing deployed.

Round 4 audit fixes on payee accounts F1-F2, dark. Read-only calls (get, list, check secrets, secret presence) are never blocked by the setup check, so the owner can see the problem; changes and routing calls still are, and the error names the payee. An unreadable stored secret_names counts as empty and is reported, never a raw error. The first fill of secret names on a payee with orders still runs the name rules and the clash check (a secret name may belong to one payee only, retired included); only the order lock is skipped. Activating or resuming a payee is refused (payee_gateway_taken, 409) while another payee is active for the same gateway and mode. Migration 0005 back-fill statements are guarded so a partial re-run cannot duplicate or rewrite. The unused package-lock.json is removed (no dependencies, CI does not use it). No money behaviour changed, nothing deployed, no flag changed.

Round 3 audit fixes on payee accounts F1-F2, dark. The secret names of a retired payee stay reserved for ever (any gateway, mode or role). While the registry flag is on, every call is refused with payee_setup_incomplete (409) if an active payee has no secret names (the legacy payee ships that way); the message says an owner must fill in the secret names first, and an owner edit that sets only the secret names of that payee is the one way out. A test shows the payee change and its audit row commit or roll back together. The bank digit rule is still 9 to 18 digits everywhere, except address_lines, number_prefix and receipt_text, where a run of exactly 6 (PIN) or 10 (phone) is allowed but any other run of 9 or more, or 6 or more digits near the words account, a/c, ifsc or iban, is refused. No money behaviour changed, nothing deployed, no flag changed.

Round 2 audit fixes on payee accounts F1-F2, dark. Bank details (account-like or card-like digit runs, IFSC, IBAN) are refused in every free-text field (error bank_detail_refused); bank_name must be letters only. payee_audit detail now holds only the names of changed fields, never text values. The identity lock also holds when a verified payment or a route points at the payee. The long-text secret screen no longer refuses long hostnames or addresses (it applies to values without spaces, dots or slashes; hex runs and key prefixes are still refused everywhere). An audit sequence clash is retried once in a fresh transaction, then fails with audit_conflict (409) and the change is rolled back. No money behaviour changed, nothing deployed, no flag changed.

Audit fix round on payee accounts F1-F2, dark. Every payee change (create, edit, activate, pause, resume, retire) now writes one hash-chained payee_audit row in the same transaction (names of secrets only, never values). Every change needs the owner role (callerType owner, real actor name); otherwise error payee_forbidden (403). Free text in checkout, invoice, note and display text is screened for pasted secret values. ctx.secrets replaces ctx.env in the secret check (documented, tested). Contract file regenerated and a test now fails if it is out of date. Owner checks before running migration 0005 on production: no test or demo marker exists in the old tables, so old orders stay mode live; and the real Razorpay secret names live in the IT Services repo, so the legacy payee still has no secret names. No money behaviour changed, nothing deployed, no flag changed.

Payee accounts, chunks F1 and F2, dark. New migration 0005 adds the payee tables and the new order columns, and back-fills every existing order, payment and tenant to the payee in use today. New src/payees.js holds the registry (create, edit, draft to active to paused to retired, identity lock after the first order, secret-name checks that never store or return a secret value). It refuses to run unless MNP_PAYEE_ACCOUNTS is 1, which is off by default, and nothing calls it yet. Credits, lots, entries and the ledger chain are unchanged. The contract file gained the new error codes. No money behaviour changed, nothing deployed, no flag changed.

Second fix round on the go-live plan after audit 1 of 0.2.1 failed on one docs Medium. Section 6, STATE.md and the PR text now say the same one rule as section 4 (no customer reaches payment until D3 items 1 to 10 and D4 pass on the same run; during D1 to D3 the flags are ON only behind the audited owner-only gate, which sits in front of the flag). Two safety checks that no test watches (spend.js lines 262 and 224) are listed honestly; later checks stop any extra money. Lock-freeze wording now covers the admin sweep (about 100 seconds worst case). preparedAt is the real commit time. Test G21 no longer depends on speed. No source code changed, no money behaviour changed, nothing deployed, no flag changed.

Fix round after two independent audits of 0.2.0. Go-live plan (docs/GO-LIVE.md) now: says plainly that the owner's Rs 1 test runs only through an owner-only gate and shows a non-owner account is refused; lists the call to IT Services inside the database transaction (freezes everything for up to 4 seconds) with its risk and fix as a gate before customers; adds the webhook address check as a gate; corrects the rollback step for missing credits (repeat rail/confirm, not credit_purchase); says a pause also refuses payment confirmations; other wording fixes. Three more safety rules are now watched by tests (46 listed guards). The log cleaner now looks at the first 2000 characters only so a huge input cannot make it slow. No money behaviour changed, nothing deployed, no flag changed.

Go-live preparation, nothing turned on. Adds docs/GO-LIVE.md (ordered steps, secret names, the owner's own Rs 1 test, flags that stay OFF, rollback). Forged or unsigned calls are now refused before they can queue on the single writer. Internal-error logs no longer carry e-mails or long secrets. The open health page asks the payment side at most once every 30 seconds. New check for any real payment-side adapter (railContract). New 'npm run guards' proves a test fails when each safety guard is removed. Also includes the console wallet module and the fixed INR pack price (in the repo since 19 Nov, never deployed) and the version files from PR 1.

First live version of the Moneypenny credit ledger on its Cloudflare Worker (code 65b86c8, deployed 19 Nov 2026 IST; time shown is that commit's time because the exact deploy time was not recorded). Built over 17 to 19 Nov 2026 from the Phase 0 build and 19 audit rounds: ledger, spend holds, price list, FX table, AI-ready API, API contract, SQLite Durable Object executor. No payment side or rate source is connected. Changes made after this code (INR fixed pack price and the console wallet module) are in the repo but not deployed; see CHANGELOG.md, Not yet deployed.
